correctness.rationale: The random choices are independent physical positions. For t>=1 the failure numerator is the sum of plane-mass powers minus twice the sum of rank-one-subspace mass powers plus eight times the zero-mass power: a tuple spanning a plane, a line, the zero space, or the whole space is counted with respective weights 1, 3-2, 7-14+8, 0. In the simplex this is 7*3^t-14. The sum of plane occupancies is 21+4c0. If c0=0 and all occupancies are at most three, they equal three; the incidence Gram matrix 2I+J and total mass seven force every nonzero multiplicity to be one. Any nonsimplex thus has a plane with at least four positions, giving failure numerator at least 4^t > 7*3^t for t>=7. For t=3 through 6, independently enumerated all 3432 nonnegative eight-tuples of total seven (2696 full rank), testing rank via an independent triple of distinct nonzero vector types with nonzero XOR. For each exact subset of physical positions, a surjection from the reads to that subset counts precisely the tuples using all of it. Summing surjection counts over deficient subsets verifies the four baseline numerators, strictness, minima 24,192,1080,5280 and precisely the 42 stated profiles at every deadline. This is different from the frozen subspace dynamic program, which was inspected, not executed. Replay: node /workspace/branches/independent-checks.js (record 3 block). For two or fewer reads spanning is impossible; rank and the tails are invariant under row-basis changes and column permutations.

evidence: v2 Theorem 5.1 gives non-strict sampled-rank optimality in every transitive matroid, so it covers the Fano plane for zero-free profiles. Replacing zero draws by independent nonzero draws can only increase rank, extending the inequality to them.
Kong et al.'s dominance condition requires restriction-rank domination, available for MDS codes; rank-three binary length-seven simplex is not MDS. Gross et al. give a sharp expectation theorem.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general v2 result is definite mathematical coverage of the non-strict order, not merely similar vocabulary. It does not determine the sharp excess probabilities. MDS and expectation optimality results do not imply these finite tails.

evidence: Kovačević v1 leaves the arbitrary deadline question open; v2 resolves it non-strictly by concavity. In the Fano special case strictness can also be recovered from v2 by checking the Hessian at uniform: on zero-sum directions the failure Hessian is a positive scalar multiple of 2*((3/7)^(t-2)-(1/7)^(t-2)) times the identity, using the incidence Gram matrix. A second maximum of the concave root of success would contradict a strict local maximum. Replacing zero draws strictly increases success for a full-rank profile with zeros, since all-zero draws can be replaced by a spanning tuple with positive probability.
The narrow four-gap claim requires a separate extremum over nonuniform integral multiplicities. Random-access sampling stops at the span containing a prescribed vector, not spanning the full space.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Do not treat the equality criterion as historically prior or as a separate major advance over v2: it has a direct additional proof using that theorem. The exact deficits and minimizer certification are not consequences of that proof, of optimizing expected time, or of a one-vector access theorem.

originality.rationale: Credit the known probability formula, t=3 optimum, and later general non-strict rank-tail theorem. The distinctive supported contribution is the explicit strict Fano comparison by deadline, in particular the exact second-place gaps and all minimizers at four deadlines; the later non-strict result comes close to the order statement but none of the inspected results determines those gaps. The expectation census has the same second-place geometry for a different objective, not the four pointwise comparisons. Record dates are not used as proof of precedence.
residual_risks: The inaccessible Delić–Ivetić full text and possibly unindexed exact rank-reliability results leave a bounded literature risk. The public expectation census was not treated as evidence about uninspected intermediate data; the exact matching expectation minimizers are disclosed. No precedence is inferred from later catalog dates.

value.rationale: Single-deadline reliability is a natural objective when the read budget is fixed; expected stopping time does not determine it. The sharp quantitative gaps and identification of every nearest competitor at the first four nontrivial deadlines give a reusable benchmark for the smallest binary projective instance and distinguish the unique optimum from its next-best multiplicity pattern. The cutoff at seven is mathematically motivated by the plane bound, not an arbitrary search horizon.
